features.description: Complete selected Class IV beran, niman and cuman indicative systems and their principal-part series.
features.scope_note: Finite morphology only; each lexical argument frame is separately stated.

features.description: Niman and cuman have their independently selected nasal-family vowel series, including Cook nōm/nōmon and cōm/cōmon and exact present singulars.
features.scope_note: Documented alternatives remain valid but do not become assigned extra recall targets.

features.description: Complete selected Class V indicative systems, including the contrast of preterite singular and plural stems.
features.scope_note: No nonfinite syntax follows from the four principal parts.

features.description: Cweðan has the checked present2/3 singular changes and ð/d alternation at its exact principal-part positions.
features.scope_note: No unrestricted consonant substitution.

features.description: Giefan has its checked palatal present and preterite series, including gēafon.
features.scope_note: Exact selected lexical series, not a universal ge- prefix or spelling rule.

features.description: Biddan, licgan and sittan have j-present geminate patterns, with exact single-consonant present2/3 singulars and their strong pasts.
features.scope_note: Present shape alone does not classify the preterite as weak.

features.description: Etan has the exact checked dental present singulars and selected long-vowel singular preterite ǣt.
features.scope_note: Accept documented alternatives with their source scope; do not extend quantity changes to unrelated verbs.

features.description: Sēon and separately evidenced gesēon have complete contracted present systems, short ie in singular2/3, and sāw-/gesāw- past plural stems.
features.scope_note: The lemma id geseon is retained; checked display quantity gesēon is an explicit new-system metadata change, not a rewrite of old source transcriptions.

features.description: Complete selected Class VI indicative systems, with the ordinary ō past and each lexical present alternation.
features.scope_note: Finite indicative only.

features.description: Slēan has the checked contracted present and selected slōg/slōgon past, retaining short ie in sliehst/sliehð.
features.scope_note: Documented slōh-type alternative is separate; no automatic creation of variant tables.

features.description: Standan retains n in the present, loses it in the strong stōd/stōdon past, and has the checked stęntst/stęnt singulars.
features.scope_note: Ordinary posture is separate from the earlier locally supplied stand-against construction.

features.description: Hębban, scieppan/gescieppan and swęrian have independently specified j-present subpatterns and strong preterites.
features.scope_note: Selected swęrie/swęrest/swęreð/swęriað does not imply that every -ian verb is weak.

features.description: Selected Class VII ēo-past systems share the preterite vowel across singular and plural while retaining distinct present systems and lexical spellings.
features.scope_note: The class name supplies a practical grouping; historical reduplication is not an additional required system.

features.description: Selected Class VII present2/3 singulars have exactly the checked vowel and consonant changes, including weaxan wiext in both persons.
features.scope_note: No universal mutation rule is inferred from the class label.

features.description: Lǣtan, hātan and fōn have the selected ē-past systems and their exact present singulars.
features.scope_note: Active hātan does not teach anomalous passive hātte, infinitive commands or naming syntax.

features.description: Fōn has its checked contracted present and nasal-stem fēng/fēngon past.
features.scope_note: Citation-only fangen does not establish a participial construction.

features.description: Geswīcan, scīnan, flēogan and swimman are new whole finite lexical systems following earlier strong I–III families.
features.scope_note: Earlier knowledge of a class, supplied geswāc, and supplied scīnen/scinen are not prior productive mastery of these systems.

features.description: Gesēon, gescieppan and geswīcan are separately evidenced lexical systems with full finite paradigms and their stated senses.
features.scope_note: No productive prefix attachment or automatic aspect/sense rule.

features.description: Beran in carry and niman in take have an accusative person/thing as their selected ordinary object.
features.scope_note: The new food/fish examples are declared ordinary lexical applications, not falsely attributed source quotations; no goal or source preposition is introduced.

features.description: Giefan gives an accusative thing to a dative recipient, with prior noun, pronoun and possessive forms.
features.scope_note: Companions and birds as recipients are declared ordinary applications; no new benefactive or clausal construction.

features.description: Sittan, licgan and standan describe ordinary intransitive posture; a previously taught locative on+dative phrase may locate the subject.
features.scope_note: No causal placement, directional complement or stand-against construction is inferred.

features.description: Etan means eat, with an accusative food object or with the food understood in an ordinary objectless use.
features.scope_note: No partitive genitive, infinitive complement or idiom of consuming something figuratively is assigned.

features.description: Sēon and gesēon take an accusative person/thing in the selected ordinary see use.
features.scope_note: Their source content clauses remain supplied; no infinitive-of-perception or general complement rule.

features.description: Feallan is used intransitively for falling.
features.scope_note: No directional preposition or transitive felling sense is implied.

features.description: Flēogan fly, scīnan shine, swimman swim and weaxan grow have their independently checked ordinary intransitive uses.
features.scope_note: Bird, star, fish and tree subjects follow the exact Cook prompts; spatial on+dative can locate the swimming without adding direction.

features.description: Slēan strike and healdan hold take an accusative person/thing in their selected ordinary physical senses.
features.scope_note: No instrumental means, command, maintaining-state complement or additional sense is inferred.

features.description: Geswīcan governs the genitive of the work/action from which the subject ceases.
features.scope_note: English from is represented by the checked governed genitive here; no unassigned fram-phrase is substituted.

features.description: Cweðan introduces direct quoted speech with an independent finite clause; quoted first-person reference belongs to the quoted speaker.
features.scope_note: Explicit extension of the earlier sęcgan quotation frame; content clauses, reported speech and requests remain outside production.

features.description: Preverbal ne applies to the selected noncontracting strong IV–VII and bridge indicative systems in ordinary negative clauses.
features.scope_note: No negative copula, contracted anomalous system, negative concord or untaught subordinate syntax.
